ov: Eel-shaped, jawless sea fish, usually about 50 cm long and dull pink to blue-grey, with loose skin and no true fins. They are the only living animals with a skull but no backbone. They eat seabed worms and burrow into dead and dying animals, and defend themselves with huge amounts of slime.

why.et: Rarely eaten in most of the world, but valued in South Korea, where it is grilled or stir-fried; one species is also eaten in Japan.

len: Usually about 50 cm; up to 127 cm
df: Seabed worms, plus dead and dying sea animals that it often enters and eats from the inside. Some hunt fish in their burrows.
fx: Its skin is sold as "eel skin" leather for wallets and belts.
It has more blood for its body mass than any other chordate.
